answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed on proven misbehavior, like a wharf charging each ship a berth bond before it may dock. A new identity starts with near-zero reputation, so at dawn of an agent's life it cannot vote or earn until it completes verified work over time. An attacker must then fund thousands of stakes and sustain them through a nebula of audits, making fake identities cost more than any reward they could extract, while honest agents earn their bond back.
